title: अंश ३ · अध्याय ९

items.speaker: और्व उवाच
items.text:
बालः कृतोपनयनो वेदाहरणतत्परः ।
गुरुगेहे वसेद्भूप ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः १ ।
items.tr:
bālaḥ kṛtopanayano vedāharaṇatatparaḥ |
gurugehe vasedbhūpa brahmacārī samāhitaḥ 1 |

items.text:
शौचा चारव्रतं तत्र कार्य्यं शुश्रूषणं गुरोः ।
व्रतानि चरता ग्राह्यो वेदश्च कृतबुद्धिना २ ।
items.tr:
śaucā cāravrataṃ tatra kāryyaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ guroḥ |
vratāni caratā grāhyo vedaśca kṛtabuddhinā 2 |

items.text:
उभे संध्ये रविं भूप तथैवाग्निं समाहितः ।
उपतिष्ठेत्तदा कुर्य्याद्गुरोरप्यभिवादनम् ३ ।
items.tr:
ubhe saṃdhye raviṃ bhūpa tathaivāgniṃ samāhitaḥ |
upatiṣṭhettadā kuryyādgurorapyabhivādanam 3 |

items.text:
स्थिते तिष्ठेद्व्रजेद्याते नीचैरासीत चासति ।
शिष्यो गुरोर्नृपश्रेष्ठ प्रतिकूलं न संचरेत् ४ ।
items.tr:
sthite tiṣṭhedvrajedyāte nīcairāsīta cāsati |
śiṣyo gurornṛpaśreṣṭha pratikūlaṃ na saṃcaret 4 |

items.text:
तेनैवोक्तं पठेद्वेदं नान्यचित्तः पुरस्स्थितः ।
अनुज्ञातश्च भिक्षान्नमश्नीयाद्गुरुणा ततः ५ ।
items.tr:
tenaivoktaṃ paṭhedvedaṃ nānyacittaḥ purassthitaḥ |
anujñātaśca bhikṣānnamaśnīyādguruṇā tataḥ 5 |

items.text:
अवगाहेदपः पूर्वमाचार्य्येणावगाहितः ।
समिज्जलादिकं चास्य काल्यं काल्यमुपानयेत् ६ ।
items.tr:
avagāhedapaḥ pūrvamācāryyeṇāvagāhitaḥ |
samijjalādikaṃ cāsya kālyaṃ kālyamupānayet 6 |

items.text:
गृहीतग्राह्यवेदश्च ततोनुज्ञामवाप्य च ।
गार्हस्थ्यमाविश्त्प्रोआ!ज्ञो निष्पन्नगुरुनिष्कृतिः ७ ।
items.tr:
gṛhītagrāhyavedaśca tatonujñāmavāpya ca |
gārhasthyamāviśtproā!jño niṣpannaguruniṣkṛtiḥ 7 |

items.text:
विधिनावाप्तदारस्तु धनं प्राप्य स्वकर्मणा ।
गृहस्थकार्य्यमखिलं कुर्य्याद्भूपाल शक्तितः ८ ।
items.tr:
vidhināvāptadārastu dhanaṃ prāpya svakarmaṇā |
gṛhasthakāryyamakhilaṃ kuryyādbhūpāla śaktitaḥ 8 |

items.text:
निवापेन पितॄनर्चन्यज्ञैर्देवांस्तथातिथीन् ।
अन्नैर्मुनींश्च स्वाध्यायैरपत्येन प्रजापतिम् ९ ।
items.tr:
nivāpena pitṝnarcanyajñairdevāṃstathātithīn |
annairmunīṃśca svādhyāyairapatyena prajāpatim 9 |

items.text:
भूतानि बलिभिश्चैव वात्सल्येनाखिलं जगत् ।
प्राप्नोति लोकान्पुरुषो निजकर्मसमार्जितान् १० ।
items.tr:
bhūtāni balibhiścaiva vātsalyenākhilaṃ jagat |
prāpnoti lokānpuruṣo nijakarmasamārjitān 10 |

items.text:
बिक्षाभुजश्च ये केचित्परिव्राड्ब्रह्मचारिणः ।
तेप्यत्रैव प्रतिष्ठंते गार्हस्थ्यं तेन वै परम् ११ ।
items.tr:
bikṣābhujaśca ye kecitparivrāḍbrahmacāriṇaḥ |
tepyatraiva pratiṣṭhaṃte gārhasthyaṃ tena vai param 11 |

items.text:
वेदाहरणकार्य्याय तीर्थस्नानाय च प्रभो ।
अटंति वसुधां विप्राः पृथिवीदर्शनाय च १२ ।
items.tr:
vedāharaṇakāryyāya tīrthasnānāya ca prabho |
aṭaṃti vasudhāṃ viprāḥ pṛthivīdarśanāya ca 12 |

items.text:
अनिकेता ह्यनाहारा यत्र सायंगृहाश्च ये ।
तेषां गृहस्थः सर्वेषां प्रतिष्ठा योनिरेव च १३ ।
items.tr:
aniketā hyanāhārā yatra sāyaṃgṛhāśca ye |
teṣāṃ gṛhasthaḥ sarveṣāṃ pratiṣṭhā yonireva ca 13 |

items.text:
तेषां स्वागतदानादिवक्तव्यं मधुरं नृप ।
गृहागतानां दद्याच्च शयनासनभोजनम् १४ ।
items.tr:
teṣāṃ svāgatadānādivaktavyaṃ madhuraṃ nṛpa |
gṛhāgatānāṃ dadyācca śayanāsanabhojanam 14 |

items.text:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्त्तते ।
स दत्त्वा दुष्कृतं तस्मै पुण्यमादाय गच्छति १५ ।
items.tr:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivarttate |
sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyamādāya gacchati 15 |

items.text:
अवज्ञानमहंकारो दंभश्चैव गृह सतः ।
परितापोपघातौ च पारुष्यं च न शस्यते १६ ।
items.tr:
avajñānamahaṃkāro daṃbhaścaiva gṛha sataḥ |
paritāpopaghātau ca pāruṣyaṃ ca na śasyate 16 |

items.text:
यस्तु सम्यक्करोत्येवं गृहस्थः परमं विधिम् ।
सर्वबंधविनिर्मुक्तो लोकानाप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् १७ ।
items.tr:
yastu samyakkarotyevaṃ gṛhasthaḥ paramaṃ vidhim |
sarvabaṃdhavinirmukto lokānāpnotyanuttamān 17 |

items.text:
वयःपरिणतो राजन्कृतकृत्यो गृहाश्रमी ।
पुत्रेषु भार्यां निक्षिप्य वनं गच्छेत्सहैव वा १८ ।
items.tr:
vayaḥpariṇato rājankṛtakṛtyo gṛhāśramī |
putreṣu bhāryāṃ nikṣipya vanaṃ gacchetsahaiva vā 18 |

items.text:
पर्णमूलफलाहारः केशश्मश्रुजटाधरः ।
भूमिशायी भवेत्तत्र मुनिस्सर्वातिथिर्नृप १९ ।
items.tr:
parṇamūlaphalāhāraḥ keśaśmaśrujaṭādharaḥ |
bhūmiśāyī bhavettatra munissarvātithirnṛpa 19 |

items.text:
चर्मकाशकुशैः कुर्य्यात्परिधानोत्तरीयके ।
तद्वत्त्रिषवणं स्नानं शस्तमस्य नरेश्वर २० ।
items.tr:
carmakāśakuśaiḥ kuryyātparidhānottarīyake |
tadvattriṣavaṇaṃ snānaṃ śastamasya nareśvara 20 |

items.text:
देवताभ्यर्चनं होमस्सर्वाभ्यागतपूजनम् ।
भिक्षाबलिप्रदानं च शस्तमस्य नरेश्वर २१ ।
items.tr:
devatābhyarcanaṃ homassarvābhyāgatapūjanam |
bhikṣābalipradānaṃ ca śastamasya nareśvara 21 |

items.text:
वन्यस्नेहेन गात्राणामभ्यंगश्चास्य शस्यते ।
तपश्च तस्य राजेंद्र शीतोष्णादिसहिष्णुता २२ ।
items.tr:
vanyasnehena gātrāṇāmabhyaṃgaścāsya śasyate |
tapaśca tasya rājeṃdra śītoṣṇādisahiṣṇutā 22 |

items.text:
यस्त्वेतां नियतश्चर्यां वानप्रस्थश्चरेन्मुनिः ।
स दहत्यग्निवद्दोषाञ्जयेल्लोकांश्च शाश्वतान् २३ ।
items.tr:
yastvetāṃ niyataścaryāṃ vānaprasthaścarenmuniḥ |
sa dahatyagnivaddoṣāñjayellokāṃśca śāśvatān 23 |

items.text:
चतुर्थश्चाश्रमो भिक्षोः प्रोच्यते यो मनीषिभिः ।
तस्य स्वरूपं गदतो मम श्रोतुं नृपार्हसि २४ ।
items.tr:
caturthaścāśramo bhikṣoḥ procyate yo manīṣibhiḥ |
tasya svarūpaṃ gadato mama śrotuṃ nṛpārhasi 24 |

items.text:
पुत्रद्र व्यकलत्रेषु त्यक्तस्नेहो नराधिप ।
चतुर्थमाश्रमस्थानं गच्छेन्निर्धूतमत्सरः २५ ।
items.tr:
putradra vyakalatreṣu tyaktasneho narādhipa |
caturthamāśramasthānaṃ gacchennirdhūtamatsaraḥ 25 |

items.text:
त्रैवर्गिकांस्त्यजेत्सर्वानारंभानवनीपते ।
मित्रादिषु समो मैत्रस्समस्तेष्वेव जंतुषु २६ ।
items.tr:
traivargikāṃstyajetsarvānāraṃbhānavanīpate |
mitrādiṣu samo maitrassamasteṣveva jaṃtuṣu 26 |

items.text:
जरायुजांडजादीनां वाड्मनःकायकर्मभिः ।
युक्तः कुर्वीत न द्रो हं सर्वसंगांश्च वर्जयेत् २७ ।
items.tr:
jarāyujāṃḍajādīnāṃ vāḍmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ |
yuktaḥ kurvīta na dro haṃ sarvasaṃgāṃśca varjayet 27 |

items.text:
एकारात्रस्थितिर्ग्रामे पंचरात्रस्थितिः पुरे ।
तथा तिष्ठेद्यथाप्रीतिर्द्वेषो वा नास्य जायते २८ ।
items.tr:
ekārātrasthitirgrāme paṃcarātrasthitiḥ pure |
tathā tiṣṭhedyathāprītirdveṣo vā nāsya jāyate 28 |

items.text:
प्राणयात्रानिमित्तं च व्यंगारे भुक्तवज्जने ।
काले प्रशस्तवर्णानां भिक्षार्थं पर्यटेद्गृहान् २९ ।
items.tr:
prāṇayātrānimittaṃ ca vyaṃgāre bhuktavajjane |
kāle praśastavarṇānāṃ bhikṣārthaṃ paryaṭedgṛhān 29 |

items.text:
कामः क्रोधस्तथा दर्पमोहलोभादयश्च ये ।
तांस्तु सर्वान्परित्यज्य परिव्राण्निर्ममो भवेत् ३० ।
items.tr:
kāmaḥ krodhastathā darpamohalobhādayaśca ye |
tāṃstu sarvānparityajya parivrāṇnirmamo bhavet 30 |

items.text:
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यश्चरते मुनिः ।
तस्यापि सर्वभूतेभ्यो न भयं विद्यते क्वचित् ३१ ।
items.tr:
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā yaścarate muniḥ |
tasyāpi sarvabhūtebhyo na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit 31 |

items.text:
कृत्वाग्निहोत्रं स्वशरीरसंस्थं शारीरमग्निं स्वमुखे जुहोति ।
विप्रस्तु भैक्ष्योपहितैर्हविर्भिश्चिताग्निकानां व्रजति स्म लोकान् ३२ ।
items.tr:
kṛtvāgnihotraṃ svaśarīrasaṃsthaṃ śārīramagniṃ svamukhe juhoti |
viprastu bhaikṣyopahitairhavirbhiścitāgnikānāṃ vrajati sma lokān 32 |

items.text:
मोक्षाश्रमं यश्चरते यथोक्तं शुचिस्सुखं कल्पितबुद्धियुक्तः ।
अनिंधनं ज्योतिरिव प्रशांतस्स ब्रह्मलोकं श्रयते द्विजातिः ३३ ।
items.tr:
mokṣāśramaṃ yaścarate yathoktaṃ śucissukhaṃ kalpitabuddhiyuktaḥ |
aniṃdhanaṃ jyotiriva praśāṃtassa brahmalokaṃ śrayate dvijātiḥ 33 |

en_chapter: Aurva said:—"O king, when a youth is invested with the sacred thread, he must reside in the house of his preceptor and study the Vedas with a concentrated mind, and leading a life of continence. He must, with pure practices, wait upon his spiritual preceptor and with the performance of religious rites acquire the Veda. He must, O king, with concentration, worship both in the morning and evening, the fire and the sun and after that he must bow to his spiritual guide. O King, he must stand when his preceptor is standing, he must move when he is walking and he must sit beneath him when he is seated; he must never sit nor walk, nor stand when his teacher does the otherwise. Whatever portion of the Vedas he shall be taught by his preceptor, he must read that with undivided mind before him. He must beg when permitted by his teacher and eat the food thus collected. He must bathe in the water which has been first used by his preceptor and every morning he must bring for him fuel, water or anything that he may require. Having thus completed his studies, he must receive dismissal from his preceptor and then enter into the order of the householder; and taking to himself with lawful ceremonies, house, wife and wealth, he must discharge to the best of his power the duties of his life. He must satisfy the manes with cakes, the celestials with sacrifices, the guests with hospitality, the Rishis with holy study, the Patriarch with progeny, the spirits with oblations and all the worlds with truthful words. By thus discharging duties a householder may attain to heaven. A householder is a refuge to those who depend upon alms for their maintenance and those who lead an itinerant life of self denial; thus the condition of the householder is the best of all. O lord, the Brāhmins travel all over the earth either for studying the Vedas or for beholding the holy places; many of them are houseless and without food and live for the night at the house at which they arrive in the evening. The householder is always a refuge to these people. O king, it is his duty to welcome them and address them kindly and to provide them, whenever they come to his house, with a bed, a seat and food. If a guest goes back disappointed from a house he leaves behind his iniquities and takes away the accumulated piety of the householder. In the house of a good man, contumely, arrogance, hypocrisy, repining, contradiction and violence are strictly prohibited: and the householder, who performs the principal duty of hospitality, is freed from all chains and attains to better stations after death.

"O king, having performed all these duties, when a householder is stricken in years, he must proceed to woods, either with his wife, or leaving her to the charge of his son. He must live there upon leaves, roots and fruits; allow his hair and beard to grow, and braid the former upon his brows and sleep upon the ground. His dress must be made of skin or of Kāsa and Kusā grasses. He must bathe thrice a day, offer oblations to the celestials and to fire and treat all his guests with hospitality. He must beg alms and give food to all creatures. He must annoint himself with such unguents as are found in the forest and while carrying on his devout practices he must endure heat and cold. He, who leading the life of a hermit, follows these rules, destroys like fire all imperfections, and attains to the region of Brahman.

"The fourth condition of life, O king, is called by the sages, that of a mendicant. I shall relate the characteristics thereof; do thou hear. O lord of men, having relinquished attachments for wife, children and other earthly objects, men leading the life of a hermit, must enter into the fourth stage of life. He must forego the three objects of life, namely pleasure, wealth and virtue either secular or religious. And regarding all with an equal eye, he must be friend to all living beings. And being devoted, he must not injure any living creature, human or brute, either in act, word, or thought and renounce all attachments. He must not live more than one night in a village and more than five nights in a city. He must live in all those places where good feeling and not animosity is created in mind. He must, for his maintenance, beg for alms at the houses of the three first castes at the time when fires have been put out and peoples have eaten. The itinerant beggar must not call anything his own and must suppress desire, anger, covetousness, pride and folly. The ascetic, who gives no cause of fear to any living creature, does not apprehend any danger from them. The Brāhmin, who, having placed the sacrificial fire in his own body, feeds that flame with the butter that is procured by alms, through the altar of his mouth, goes to his own proper abode. But the Brāhman who longs for final emancipation, who has got a pure heart, and whose mind is perfected by self-investigation, goes to the region of Brahman, which is quiet and is as bright as the flameless smoke".
